The test image shows a close-up of stem tissue with:
- White/cottony fluffy mycelial growth
- Numerous small black specks scattered across the tissue (sclerotia)
- Bleached, pale stem tissue

This strongly points to **White Mold**. Let me confirm with the reference image.

The reference confirms: White Mold shows white fluffy mycelial growth on stems with black sclerotia. The test image is a macro close-up showing:
- White cottony/fluffy mycelium covering bleached stem tissue
- Black sclerotia (small black specks) embedded within the white mold — perfectly matching the diagnostic description: "black sclerotia embedded within white fluffy mold on stem lesions"

The pattern of scattered black sclerotia within white mycelial mass is the hallmark feature of White Mold.

```json
{"prediction": "White_Mold", "confidence": 0.92, "reasoning": "Macro close-up of stem tissue showing white fluffy/cottony mycelial growth with numerous small black sclerotia embedded within, on bleached stem tissue. This is the classic diagnostic presentation of White Mold (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum) — 'characteristic black sclerotia embedded within white fluffy mold on stem lesions.' The scattered black dots are sclerotia, not the linear pycnidia rows of Diaporthe or the microsclerotia pattern of Charcoal Rot."}
```
